utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to raise one practical matter. We moved our usual Wednesday session on the 12th of November to the 14th of November, making the 12th of November a non-sitting day. That was born out of necessity, it was the scheduling of the Appeals Chamber and the Hadzic Chamber. Now it turns out that it's not necessary any further and the Chamber would very much like to go back to Wednesday, the 12th, and not to sit on Friday, the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if the parties have great problems with that, we'd like to hear from you; but otherwise, we would like to move back to what is our ordinary weekly routine - that is, to sit Monday up to Friday. I see that Mr. Mladic would like to consult. Mr. Stojanovic, if you're ready, you may continue your examination-in-chief, but not until after I have reminded the witness. You, Mr. Bojanovic, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. And you announced that you would need another five minutes, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at D747 in e-court, please, paragraph 5. D747, paragraph 5 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, while we're waiting for the page to upload, let's just say that you're saying there that military tribunals were formed with the corps commands and that it was their responsibility to cover the areas of responsibilities of the corps. Please, tell the Trial Chamber the military court that you worked for, the one in Bijeljina, what territory did it cover?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My court covered the area to the west, so that it partially affected the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we are having interference. We cannot hear the witness properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: He might be coming too close to the microphone so there are interruptions. We cannot hear everything that he is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please move slightly away from the microphone. Let's try it again because the interpreters had some problems. You started and what is recorded until now is that you said so that it partially affected the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps. Could you please resume from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Other than this area of responsibility, the court was responsible for the area of responsibility of the East Bosnia Corps and the Krajina Corps which was formed in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 7 of your statement, which you have in front of you, Mr. Bojanovic, you discuss the composition of the military court and the prosecutor's office. So I would like you to tell the Trial Chamber whether this composition remained the same throughout the war or did the personnel vary?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first composition was Mr. Mirko Vasiljevic, he was the president, myself, and Jezdimir Spasovic [phoen]. We were the judges. Then later after about half a year or so Ljubisa Kitic arrived. And then after him Damjan Kaurinovic joined us. I left the court in September 1993, Jezdimir Spasovic left a year later. We were replaced by Luka Borovcanin, I think, and Dusko Bojic. When we're talking about the prosecutor's office responsible for the East Bosnia Corps, Predrag Ninic was the prosecutor and Goran Blagojevic was the deputy. In late 1992 Momir Radulovic became the deputy. After I left from I think in 1994, late 1994, Dusko Panic became the deputy military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at paragraph 14 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Stojanovic, I don't know whether there's any translation issue but -- or that my knowledge of the English language is not sufficient, but could you invite the witness to repeat or to tell us, perhaps in different wording, what we find in the last three lines of paragraph 7, starting in English with "I have provided the names ..." because the meaning of that part of his statement is not entirely clear to me. Could you invite the witness to either explain or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, in line with His Honour's suggestion, could you please tell us, regarding the names that you mentioned from the prosecutor's office, these last three names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it reads in English: "I have provided the names of military judges and prosecutors in this statement because ..." and then there comes an explanation which is at least not clear to me. So the last three lines, not the last three bullet points, but the last three lines, whether the witness could tell us, perhaps in his own wording, what he meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I understand, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, in the last paragraph of paragraph 7 you say that at that time there were no more professionally qualified or more suitable persons than the above-mentioned. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to begin his answer again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please make a pause between question and answer because when you start your answer the interpreters are still explaining to us in English what the question was and they miss part of your answer. So perhaps the best way would be that you slowly repeat your -- the last two lines in the original because it may be that we get a different answer. I guess we do, Mr. Stojanovic, because the way in which you put the question was to some extent already resolving the problem. Could I invite you to slowly read the last two lines of paragraph 7, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I provide in my statement the names of the judges and the prosecutors because I believe that in the area of responsibility of the corps there were no more better professionally qualified or suitable persons than those that I named. This is what it's about. When the military courts were formed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I just sought clarification of the answer. What still puzzles me is to say you mentioned the members of the court, the judges and the prosecutors, because there were no better persons. I thought that you would mention those who were appointed, and then perhaps a second step is that you think that they were appointed because there were no more qualified persons. That is what I would understand. Is that what you intended to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And just to complete I would like us to look at paragraph 14 of your statement. In the paragraph you comment on one of the cases that you processed and you say that you issued an order for a warrant of arrest to be issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like us to look at document 1D00831. This is the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you mean this order when you mentioned what you said in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document. As far as I can remember, I scheduled the main hearing in this case twice, and both times I was informed by the post office that the summons could not be delivered to the accused because he was in Switzerland. So I proceeded in accordance with the criminal law by issuing an order on the 21st of February, 1993, that the -- their warrant of arrest should be issued for the fugitive.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bojanovic, for this clarification of what was in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps now is a good moment to tender document 65 ter 1D00831. And by your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read out the other exhibits that we would like to be associated with the statement of this witness, Mr. Savo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Stojanovic, I see that the witness is in his statement referring to 1D25456. I find that number as a Karadzic 65 ter number and it is apparently corresponding with the Mladic 65 ter number 1D03106 on your list, on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're correct, Your Honour. That's 1D031 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware that you now gave another number, but what I would like to know is: What then appears under number 1D03106, where that mistake comes from, and what then may have happened during the interview of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all extra microphones be switched off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of this witness. Mr. Stojanovic, could you tell us what we find if we would look at 1D03106? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You would practically have the entire case file of the military court in Bijeljina in the case of Rade Mihajlovic, containing a number of orders, a number of judgements that were made in that case and, among other things, this order that we are discussing now. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You say it's a broader case file. Witness, what was shown to you when you gave your statement and what you referred to in paragraph 14? Was the whole of the file shown to you or was it just your wanted circular that was shown to you? Or don't you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have an order on the monitor on the warrant of arrest which was issued on the 21st of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have D747, paragraph 14 on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please switch off your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You commented there on a document known by the number 1D25456. What was shown to you when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was shown the order on the issuance of the warrant of arrest or the wanted circular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Stojanovic, the cover page of the -- oh no, I'm sorry. You were interviewed in July of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you interviewed in any other case before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the Radovan Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you sought a document to be admitted into evidence. No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D831 receives number D748, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. No, I think that's the only document you would like to have in evidence, isn't it, Mr. Stojanovic? Oh, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, I would like to tender a few more documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I may have been confused. What I said at this moment is you want to limit yourself to the detention order and not the whole file. And now we move on to any other associated exhibits you would like to tender. Mr. Stojanovic, could you name them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender 65 ter document 1D03105, which accompanies paragraph 11 of the witness statement. And by your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read out the other exhibits that I would like to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one unless there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic was kind enough to provide me with a list at the end of the session yesterday. We have no objections to any of the eight that he's tendering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Then next one, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document, 1D03107 which goes with paragraph 23 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02328, that goes with paragraph 24 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02332, which corresponds to paragraph 24 once again of the witness statement. Then 1D02333 corresponding to paragraph 25 of the witness statement. Then 1D02334 corresponding to paragraph 26 of the witness statement. And two more documents that correspond to paragraph 27 of the witness statement, those being 1D02335 and 1D02336. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I have now eight documents. I'll read their numbers. Madam Registrar, if you would immediately then give the number assigned. The first one is 1D03105.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D749, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Next one is 1D03107.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D750, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02328.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D751, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02332.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D752, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02333.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D753, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02334.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D754, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02335.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D755, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D02336.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D756, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and I would like to thank the witness. I have no more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- before I give an opportunity to Mr. Traldi to cross-examine you, Judge Fluegge has one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, we saw on the screen one circular for arrest warrant, it was about a murder case. What was, just in brief, the factual background? Why was this person wanted for murder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Due to the fact that he was not accessible to the military judiciary organs, I scheduled the main hearing twice and twice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we could not deliver the summons to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand that, but this was not my question. It was a murder case. What kind of murder, alleged murder, took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rado Mihajlovic, the accused, in 1992 - I'm not sure about the date but I think it was in September - he killed somebody in the barracks dormitory. I don't remember the name of the victim but it was a Muslim person. And he allowed the special guards units during capture of an important military facility to enter through certain passages and the police came back to the barracks after the operation with the unit. Rado Mihajlovic, the accused, once - I think it was September - killed him in the barracks dormitory in Bijeljina. That was the -- those were the counts in the indictment, that's what he was charged with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Just one question: Was the victim a detainee or a soldier in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he was not a detainee. He was sleeping in the dorm when he was killed with the rest of the unit -- soldiers from that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I nevertheless have one follow-up question there. You say it was in September 1992. Was Mr. Mihajlovic, was he a member of the armed forces of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was. He was a member of that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the victim was sleeping in the dormitory of that same unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber has received quite some evidence about the composition of the armed forces on both sides and we also learned that there were not many Muslims serving in the armed forces of the Republika Srpska. You said the victim was a Muslim. Do you know anything about the background why this Muslim stayed within the Republika Srpska armed forces or why he joined that, because that's -- well, not the common thing that happened at the time as far as we learned from the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 on the western slopes of Mount Majevica there was a Serbian enclave of three villages that had been surrounded for a few months, surrounded by the Muslim armed forces. I think that Smoluca, Podpec, and Tinja were the names of these villages. A special unit of the Eastern Bosnian Corps, I think in the month of August, managed to lift that blockade and to get the civilian population out of this Serb enclave. A person was from that area and managed to get the special unit through, and then after that operation he stayed with that unit until the killing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, that Muslim assisted in the -- in deblocking the Muslim blockade of a Serb enclave and after he had done that he stayed with the Republika Srpska, the VRS? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You'll find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to start with a few brief questions about the structure and functioning of your court. I'm going to begin with your appointment to the court. You say that you and some others were taken to the corps command in Ugljevik in July 1992 to interview for positions at the Bijeljina military court. The corps command to which you are referring is the command of the East Bosnia Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you say you and some others were recommended to be military judges by the competent VRS command, again you're speaking of the command of the East Bosnia Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your court would compile reports on its work; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those would be submitted to the supreme military court; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the supreme military court would also compile reports on its work, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know to whom those reports were submitted?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and the government, or rather, the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the Main Staff, you mean specifically the sector for, if I recall correctly, legal, moral, and religious affairs?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the military prosecutor's offices, like the military courts, were attached to the relevant corps commands; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there was a supreme military prosecutor's office attached to the Main Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you said a moment ago that the East Bosnia Corps command recommended your appointment. Do you know to whom they made that recommendation?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I just know that in the summer of 1992 I was called to the barracks at Bijeljina to go to Ugljevik with a number of colleagues, and I think there was a conversation with the representatives of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall which representatives of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really cannot remember. It was a long time ago. I just know that General Govedarica -- no, Colonel Govedarica, I think that was his name, was in a way the co-ordinator of the military courts and he often came to see us on behalf of the Main Staff. I don't know whether he attended that meeting in Ugljevik. I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who was it that finally signed your appointment?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I next have two questions about sentencing. First, your court followed a sentencing policy which was decided on during joint meetings of the judges of the court in contact with the supreme military court; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, only a sentence of five years or more triggered a mandatory requirement for detention; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the law prescribes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 5 of your statement you say that the military courts were formed with the corps commands and their jurisdictions covered the zones of responsibility of the VRS corps. You discussed this at transcript page 3 today and I'm returning to it to clarify the record. It's right that when you first became a judge your court had jurisdiction over the East Bosnia Corps zone of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at first. However, very soon it turned out that, as I've already mentioned when I first started testifying, our area of responsibility went to the river Bosna in the west - rather, the town of Doboj - and also the area of Podrinje, later on the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps which I think was established in September that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was asking because you'd been recorded earlier as saying that when the Krajina Corps was established in September 1991 that became part of your jurisdiction. In fact, it was when the Drina Corps was established at the end of October 1992, right, that you acquired jurisdiction over the Drina Corps area?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you refer to jurisdiction being based on zones of responsibility. If a soldier from the Herzegovina Corps was fighting in Vlasenica as part of a joint operation and committed a crime, which court would have had jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness. Please do not come very close to the microphone but speak in the direction of the microphone, because the interpreters are unable to hear you. Perhaps the usher could assist and let's give it another try. The question was: "If a soldier from the Herzegovina Corps was fighting in Vlasenica as part of a joint operation and committed a crime, which court would have had jurisdiction?" Could you answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military court in Bijeljina would be in charge since territorial jurisdiction was based on where the crime had been committed, not on the affiliation of a particular soldier with a particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now, sir, to the cases discussed in your statement. First the Rade Mihajlovic case which you also discussed this morning and which you discuss in paragraph 14. Mr. Mihajlovic was charged with killing a Muslim named Enes Tabakovic in the Vojvoda Stepa Stepanovic barracks in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you testified this morning that Mr. Tabakovic was not a detainee there. The military court documents in the case did refer to him as a detainee, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we go into private session for a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Remaining on the Mihajlovic case, sir, Mr. Mihajlovic was in custody for much of the investigation but he was released before he was indicted; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your involvement in the case was basically just to issue the wanted notice this morning after he'd become a fugitive; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I got that case and I was supposed to carry out the entire procedure and I was supposed to pass the judgement in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Basically the only thing you did in the case was to issue a wanted notice because he was a fugitive; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is nothing else I could have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say in paragraph 14 of your statement that you do not know about the further fate of the case. In fact, he was only eventually convicted in absentia in 2001; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learned that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you learn that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned that when preparing to testify in the case of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you gave your statement in this case, you were interviewed, the 14th of July of this year; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I read in that statement that you do not know about the further fate of this case. If you learned it during your preparation for the Karadzic testimony, you would have known on the 14th of July about the further fate of this case, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that that was not relevant for this testimony because I did not take any other action in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it was irrelevant, you could have left it out. You can't say "I don't know the fate" if you do know, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. You are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, I'm talking about facts and apparently you have not corrected it at any later stage. Mr. Traldi. May I warn you to really to perhaps even carefully re-read your statement and consider whether everything is true, not whether it's relevant or not. It's a very bad excuse to say: I considered it irrelevant. If it's irrelevant, don't mention it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to address two more cases briefly before the break. In your statement you discuss a case number IK11393 involving Petar Trifkovic and others. I only have one question about it: None of the accused in that case received a sentence of five years or more, did they?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, which paragraph of the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it 23 you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That sounds right according to my memory, but I'm afraid I didn't note it this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's the number of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you both, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have a few brief questions about the Tasovac case, which we discuss -- which you discuss, rather, in paragraph 24. Now, first, I'd like to set out briefly the facts and ask you to confirm that I have them right. Mr. Tasovac met some ethnic Croat civilians on the street. He said: "You motherfucking Ustasha, I'll kill you now." And then when one started to run away, Mr. Tasovac shot at him twice and killed him in front of his wife and his mother. Is that a correct statement of the facts of the case?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This was on the 1st of September, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I carried out the investigation in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was detained for three days and then released on the 4th of September, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A death certificate for the victim wasn't even issued until June of 1993, was it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, there was no conviction until after you left the military court; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't remember. I just know that he received four and a half years in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge as to how much time he actually spent in prison?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to turn to another case. I think that one will take me more than the minute or two we have before the break, and so for continuity I'd suggest that we break a little bit early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We then take the break now. Witness, we would like to see you back in 20 minutes. We take a break. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, could I verify whether there are any compelling reasons not to sit on Wednesday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will sit on the 12th of November and we'll not sit on Friday, the 14th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Next, sir, in paragraph 11 of your statement you discuss the Cvetkovic and Jurosevic case and the transfer of the suspects to the judicial authorities in Brcko. You corrected the date in this paragraph yesterday at transcript page 27929. Can we assume you reviewed this paragraph carefully in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, considering that correction you say that on the 30th of October, 1992, you were contacted by the person on duty at the military court and told that the military police apprehended two people suspected of raping two Muslim women in Brcko. You mention that the same evening you took statements from the victims, interrogated the suspects, and ordered their detention; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we briefly move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you met with Mr. Cvetkovic on the 29th of October, 1992, you specifically interviewed him about this murder case; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, evidently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while in your statement you say that he was not a member of the military when he committed the rapes, he was a member of the VRS when he allegedly committed this murder; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is -- actually, we established that he was not a member of the armed forces. At the time that he committed the killing, he was a volunteer. We established that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 1D02311.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up in the English this is a record of an interview of Mr. Cvetkovic, and at the top it refers to the crime, Article 36, paragraph 2, that's murder; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And under "present" we see below investigating investigating judge Captain Savo Bojanovic; that's you yourself, correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 4 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S, the third paragraph from the bottom in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a note that during the interview the accused presented the court with a certificate issued by military post 7410 on 13th of October, 1992, in Brcko, which shows that he was in the 7th Novi Sad Company from 21 June to 19 September 1992. That included the time when he allegedly co-perpetrated the murder; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you testified in the Karadzic case that you weren't aware that Mr. Cvetkovic and Mr. Jurosevic were charged with murder. In fact, clearly you'd been aware of it for more than two decades; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid that I forgot that because so much time had passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the day after this interrogation, the 30th of October, 1992, the investigation was expanded to include the multiple rapes that you discuss in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the rapes were believed to have been perpetrated by Mr. Cvetkovic, not by Mr. Jurosevic; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you released both of them before completing your investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were released from detention due to the fact that the date had expired for them to be kept in detention. I think that the period of time that had expired was 60 days. I'm not sure. And since there was no request by the prosecutor to extend the detention by another three months, I had to release them. The supreme military court would also have been able to prolong the detention for an additional 90 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And detention could be prolonged under the law because of the nature of the crimes they were suspected of; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And neither Mr. Cvetkovic nor Mr. Jurosevic was convicted during the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to make sure the record pellucidly clear, you've agreed with me that neither one was corrected -- was convicted during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learned that proceedings were conducted against them after the war before a court in Brcko in view of the fact that they were not under the jurisdiction of the military court, and I think that Cvetkovic is being processed before the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2311 receives number P6894, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraphs 25 through 27 of your statement you discuss a number of cases involving instances of theft by members of the VRS. Now, your court applied a particular policy that a suspended sentence had sufficient effect in such cases; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a technical problem. I cannot hear. I didn't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, can you hear me speaking now?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraphs 25 through 27 of your statement you discuss a number of cases involving instances of theft by members of the VRS. Your court applied a particular policy that a suspended sentence had sufficient effect in such cases; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When these crimes are concerned, our --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. We're having a lot of difficulty hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please speak more slowly because the interpreters are unable to follow you. Could you please resume from where you said "when these crimes are concerned ..." and then you continued and that was on a question about the policy of suspended sentences to be applied in cases of theft by members of the VRS. Could you resume from there, when these crimes are concerned, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We took the position in sentencing for these types of crimes that suspended sentences would have the same effect of punishment due to the fact that all the perpetrators were members of the Army of Republika Srpska and by pronouncing or passing a proper sentence we would damage the working power of the JNA -- of the army, so that is why we took the position that a suspended sentence would be more effective for these types of crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I have questions about the few of the cases that you discuss in your statement. Regarding the correct -- the case against Milan Peric, it's correct that the alleged victim of the theft was in fact a publicly owned company; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a state-owned company and that was the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 1D02339.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this will be the judgement in the case against Cviko and Milorad Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 2 in the English and the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this judgement in the paragraph below the words "are guilty" refers to the conviction of these people for taking property from "several abandoned houses of unknown owners." Now, you don't mention in your statement that the property they were convicted of stealing was abandoned when they took it, do you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. And I'll rephrase to be as clear as possible. In your statement you say these convictions were for theft of Muslim property. You don't mention that in this case the property they were convicted of stealing had already been abandoned by its owners; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says from a number of abandoned houses of unknown owners they are responsible ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The interpretation stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you were explaining that it says in the judgement that this property came from a number of abandoned houses of unknown owners. Could you repeat any further explanation that you just provided?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were abandoned houses of unidentified owners from a place called Tursunovo Brdo, which was inhabited exclusively by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was a village in Ugljevik municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's actually the hamlet of Teocak. It's part of the village of Teocak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 4 in the English and the bottom of page 2 in the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while we do, I think His Honour Judge Moloto may have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Actually for you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi, you started asking the witness about the case against Milan Peric, who was supposed to have stolen from a company victim. And then you called for this exhibit which deals with other people. I'm trying to connect the Milan Peric case with what you are following and can you -- I'm not quite sure whether you are done with the Peric case or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. What I'm doing is going through some of the cases addressed in paragraph 27 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- which he refers to as convictions for theft of movable property belonging to individuals of Croat and Muslim ethnicities. Related to the Peric case my only question was: This was a socially owned company that he was convicted of stealing from; right. And I've turned now to the next case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm sorry for not being more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, we're now at page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have the bottom of page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's describing the arguments by the defendants.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the end of paragraph -- of the second paragraph from the top in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The defendants say in part that these properties would have burned when the houses at Tursunovo Brdo were burned. The houses at Tursunovo Brdo were in fact burned after they were abandoned; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document. It was initially an associated exhibit. I'm happy to have either a D or a P number depending on Mr. Stojanovic's preference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not want to tender this document precisely for these reasons, but as far as I am concerned I think that it would be more logical for the document to be admitted as a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand. I'm fine with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by exactly for these reasons?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, precisely for the reasons that I tried to reduce my list of exhibits, I did not tender this document. This is actually one of the documents that I did not tender, but I confirm that the document was originally on that first list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One question, where the witness states that property was stolen in the Peric case from Croat and Muslim -- persons of Croat and Muslim ethnicity, whereas the document apparently tells us that it was a socially owned company. Mr. Stojanovic, why when you apparently have shown this document to the witness, why didn't you tell him that what he told you is contradicted by the document you have shown him? And I'm now returning to the Peric case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. During proofing of the witness I did go through that judgement with the witness. I asked him: Why is this an argument for the thesis that he put forward. He informed me that this was a company that was in the town of Brcko, the part that belonged to the Muslims. And then I said: It's better not to go with that, that the assertion was too broad, and that was the reason why I decided not to tender this document as part of the argument for what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are convinced and if you have put to the witness that what he stated in his statement is not in line with the document you've shown him, then the appropriate action is not not to tender that document. The appropriate action is to correct the statement so that it is truthful again rather than of dubious truth. Would you please keep that in mind whenever you proof a witness again, that you should have changed the statement or you should have at least adopted something in the proofing note and not just not to tender the document. That's not the appropriate way of proceeding. I leave it to that for the time being. Mr. Traldi, you're still waiting for the number, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am for 1D02339.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, you may give it a P number because that's the preference of Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2339 receives P6895, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 1D02337.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be the Arsenic case which you also mention in paragraph 27 and the judgement in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 2 in the English and again page 1 below the word "guilty" or "is guilty" in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see that Mr. Arsenic was also convicted of stealing property from several houses of unknown owners in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 5 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see at the bottom of the third paragraph in the English and the first paragraph in the first paragraph in the B/C/S that "the earlier owners of the items had been forced to leave their homes due to the war." Now, your evidence is that those people were Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a part of town of Brcko that is called Klanac where Muslims lived and it was in the zone of war operations, and all the inhabitants of that area had already left their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 4 in the English and 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we're going to see on much of this page is a description of what the accused said in his defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page in the English and the bottom of the third paragraph from the bottom in the B/C/S, we see that he said:

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "That the command of his unit did not approve such conduct. On the contrary, it was forbidden to take war booty home." Now, the property that he was convicted of stealing was supposed to be treated as war booty, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no war booty during this war as far as I know. The point was to defend and protect everybody's property during this war, including in the zone of war operations and that is confirmed by this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you don't recall then what the Republika Srpska regulations at the time said should be done with war booty?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I was not aware of any such regulations and the other judges in the military court weren't aware of that either. This was an unknown category.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd put to you that the regulations at the time were that war booty was supposed to go to the state reserves; that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, regarding the other cases that you discuss in this paragraph, the Bozidar Petrovic and Branko Lukic cases, the property stolen in those cases was also described as having been abandoned by its Muslim owners; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: They too had left the areas where these operations were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, on the topic of the theft cases, I've reviewed these cases in some detail. None of the judgements say: We're only imposing a suspended sentence because of our court's policy regarding theft cases, do they?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that cannot be stated in a judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So where they refer instead to mitigating factors, that was an attempt to conceal the policy that the judges had agreed on to apply only suspended sentences in those cases; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your position. That's not the way it is. I don't think that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, then I'll give you an opportunity to explain. You said something like that cannot be stated in a judgement. It can't be stated in a judgement because it has to be concealed; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In a judgement one cannot state the position of the court with regard to penal policy. We at chambers sessions adopted that position but we did not include it in the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 1D02337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2337 receives number P6896, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31555.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an armed rebellion case; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The accused is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was sentenced to 12 years in prison, that's longer than the sentence in any of the cases you discuss in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were lengthier prison sentences than this one, I'm sure, but I can explain what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether this is a sentence longer than in any of the cases you have dealt with in your statement, not whether there have been lengthier sentences which you do not deal with. But is this the longer -- is this longer than any of the sentences you discuss in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31555 receives number P6897, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to change topics now and turn to Batkovic camp. Batkovic was under the jurisdiction of the East Bosnia Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a military remand prison is where people who are going to be charged with a crime in the military justice system are held; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had our own detention unit within the military court and persons who were detained by the military court were held in that detention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So Batkovic was not a military remand prison; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to keep the record clear, that's no, it wasn't a military remand prison; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So in general, not exclusively but in general, the people who were being charged with armed rebellion or with any other crime would have been held at the military remand prison, not at Batkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot understand what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You've been asked to repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off and could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone and to speak clearly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you come a bit closer to the microphone and could you also try to speak clearly so that your words are not lost. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question, sir. In general the people who were being charged with armed rebellion or with any other crime would have been held at the military remand prison, not at Batkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the person mentioned here Izet, he was not detained, he was already in Batkovic when an indictment was issued against him; that is to say that he was not in the detention unit of the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you never visited Batkovic in your official capacity; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document, by the way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you did, however, go to visit people detained there; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times. Five or six times for sure I went to Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now your kum was detained there; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. My kum who lives in Bijeljina is a Muslim and some of his friends, Muslims who lived abroad in Germany and Austria, asked him to take cigarettes, food, letters to Batkovic to other people who were held there. And now because of our relationship I went to Batkovic and took cigarettes, food, and letters to these persons. He never went there. He lives in Bijeljina and he lived in Bijeljina throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the detainees you visited there were Muslim civilians, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31393.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraph 18 of your statement you say that the Red Cross "supervised the Ekonomija collection centre," that's what's known as Batkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this document comes from the Main Staff to the command of the Drina Corps and is dated 8 October 1993. And I think we're having -- we're taking a moment to get the B/C/S up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could have just a second, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registrar tells me we have a technical problem, but apparently it's there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this document comes from the Main Staff to the command of the Drina Corps. It's dated the 8th of October, 1993. Directing your attention to the lower part of the page we see a reference to a ten-member Red Cross team which will be visiting prisoners in Batkovici and the order says: "Please notify the administration of the centre in Batkovici, Ministry of the Interior organs, and the local authorities." So the truth is that camp authorities would be notified like this, before the Red Cross came to visit; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31393 receives number P6898, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now, sir, to the case at Vanekov Mlin discussed in paragraph 18 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- where two detainees were murdered and one was beheaded by VRS soldiers who had stopped to refuel their vehicles. Those detainees were detained in Batkovic camp at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Vanekov Mlin was across the street from a VRS barracks in Bijeljina; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the other side of the entrance into the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which barracks was that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only barracks in Bijeljina, Vojvoda Stepa Stepanovic, that's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know what units were accommodated in that barracks?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In 1993, specifically February of 1993 when you conducted the investigation into this murder.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were units of the Eastern Bosnian Corps, that is where the command of the military police was stationed and they assisted us, the military judges, during investigations; but which units they were exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you don't know if anyone was ever punished for the murders at Vanekov Mlin, do you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you do know that no one was punished during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know, believe me, whether anybody was punished after the war either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you describe in your statement the steps you took, you collected photo documentation, did interviews, decided to initiate an investigation, and issued a wanted circular for an unidentified perpetrator. You don't know if any effort beyond that was ever made to identify the 2nd Krajina Corps soldiers who committed this crime, do you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to tell you that I did not decide to initiate investigation. I carried out an on-site investigation, that is what I was in charge of. As for record and photo documentation, I submitted that to the office of the prosecutor and then they were to initiate an investigation because the perpetrator was not known and I carried out the on-site investigation during the night. The next day when I came to work at the CSB Bijeljina a wanted notice was issued, person unknown, but probably a soldier of the 2nd Krajina Brigade. The rest was not within the purview of the court but the police. They were supposed to act on the wanted notice and they were supposed to bring in the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the perpetrator's a soldier so when you say the police you mean the military police; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the MUP and the centre of public security of Bijeljina that was in charge and that actually offered logistical assistance in such cases to the court in Bijeljina. The military police did not have such powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These were soldiers. It was early 1993. Based on your evidence, the military justice system had jurisdiction whether they were -- whether they had committed the crime on or off duty; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment we still did not have an accurate position with regard to subject matter jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you're going beyond your one-hour estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, my estimate was two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, then I stand corrected. If that -- yes, two hours. Then I was -- I have not taken sufficient notice of the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I can say I expect rather than going beyond it to be a bit below it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I at this moment put an additional question to the witness. A minute ago you at the beginning of a longer answer you said: "First of all, I have to tell you that I did not decide to initiate investigation. I carried out an on-site investigation. That's what I was in charge of." That was your answer. When I read your statement in paragraph 18, the penultimate paragraph, third sentence I read: "I made a decision on initiating the investigating proceedings and issued a wanted circular for an unknown perpetrator." Can you explain what you mean -- can you please explain why you said that you did not decide to initiate investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this must be a mistake in my statement. I just issued a wanted notice because the record and the photo documentation, all of that I provided to the Eastern Bosnia Corps and they were supposed to act on that. I think that that statement of mine was mistranslated in that section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that. Could a check be made over the next break of the relevant line in the B/C/S and the English translation. Madam Registrar, could you organise that just this line, whether it could be verified, whether there's any mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you say this brigade had stopped to fill their vehicles with fuel. Did you determine if a record was created of the fuel being provided to them during your investigation?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was not in dispute because buses that drove soldiers from the Drina front line stopped and the soldiers got out while the buses got into the barracks and went to the gasoline station to get gasoline. And the killings took place as the buses were being fuelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you determine what unit in the brigade had been there filling up their buses with fuel?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that it was a unit from the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the 2nd Krajina Corps at the time would have had a number of units, clearly a fairly large number of units; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the receipt for the fuel wouldn't just have said "2nd Krajina Corps unit unidentified," would it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I didn't check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you didn't make an effort to identify what unit the perpetrators were from?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police was supposed to do that on my orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you don't know if they ever did?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Clearly the military courts were aware of these murders. Was the Batkovic camp command also notified since it was people detained there who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. On the third day a delegation of the International Red Cross came. They were supervising Batkovic. They came to attend a meeting with me and Momir Radulovic, deputy prosecutor, attended the meeting too. I made them aware of the on-site investigation report, everything I collected, and also the order to issue a wanted notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was the corps command notified that this murder had taken place? And I'm speaking first of the East Bosnia Corps command.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not understand what the witness was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, could you please repeat your answer and perhaps speak up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, there was no duty to inform the corps command because the military judiciary was not subordinated to the Eastern Bosnia Corps. Believe me, we did not send such reports for other crimes either that we dealt with, or rather, that we tried.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're familiar with Article 142 of the Criminal Code; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to remind me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. That's the article dealing with war crimes against the civilian population, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there wasn't a single Article 142 prosecution before the Bijeljina military court of a VRS soldier for crimes against non-Serbs during the entire war, was there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was at the military court, until the end of 1993, there were none, and I think that I really didn't hear of any such cases being tried after that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we're at the time for the break. I note I'll be only about 10 or 15 minutes afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you stay well within the time-limits you announced, Mr. Traldi. Could the witness already follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take that break, I asked the translation - not the interpretation in court - but the translation of the one line in the statement to be verified, which is: "I made a decision on initiating the investigation proceedings and issued a wanted circular for an NN perpetrator." That is the line we're interested in. Mr. Stojanovic or Mr. Lukic, I'm addressing you. Of course we don't have to bother the CLSS with the issue if you agree that the English version corresponds with the B/C/S version. Then we don't have to bother them. Then I'll put to the witness that -- the witness suggested that the original did not include the words that he had decided that investigations would be initiated. Because if you agree that the translation is accurate -- I don't know who made the translation of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you can just allow us to let you know after the break because then we can just look at the original and compare it to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, may I take it that you have the original available? If not, we'll put it on the screen right away so that you can verify it at this moment. We can't wait until after the break because I want to put to the witness if he's correct I want to invite those responsible for the translation to apologise to the witness for the bad translation. If, however, he's blaming others for what he should have clearly seen in the original, then I may use other language. Could you please check. I think the statement is D747 if I'm not mistaken and could we have that on our screen. Could we have paragraph 18 in both languages --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just -- just bear with me for one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, it's on the B/C/S version the third paragraph from the bottom, the third sentence which is the second and the third line of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what we'd like to know is whether the original does not state that the witness made a decision on initiating the investigation proceedings. Does it appear in the original or does it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It states in the original, Your Honours: "I issued a decision on initiating the investigation proceedings and issued a wanted circular for an NN perpetrator."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I may have to use other language than apologies. Under those circumstances, there seems to be no dispute. Who prepared the translation, Mr. Stojanovic? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the translation was taken from the Karadzic case because it's a statement that is identical to what was said in the Karadzic case except for minor corrections that the witness provided to our investigator regarding his own personal status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may explain a few matters. So that was done at the 14th of July where he was interviewed and where we read that this is the statement resulting from this interview. We take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I just want to introduce Mr. Jason File who is assisting Mr. Traldi with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, before you proceed I must say I just have a question to put to the witness. Sir, just before the break at page 46, line 12, you were asked the question: "So you didn't make an effort to identify what unit the perpetrators were from?" You said: "The police was supposed to do that on my orders." The next question was: "And you don't know if they ever did?" You said: "I don't know." My question to you is: Did you quiz the police why they didn't obey your order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not because I was not in charge of that investigation. After conducting the on-the-scene investigation, I sent the request to the prosecutor's office who then in turn submitted a request.
